newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Sears sees steep profit fall.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Sears sees steep profit fall.

text.p: British retailer Sears Plc on Tuesday reported a steep fall in first half profits as provisions for asset sales and bad debts virtually wiped out earnings.
There is no connection between Sears Plc and Hoffman Estates, Ill.-based Sears, Roebuck and Co.
Pretax profit including the provisions was 2.5 million pounds ($3.9 million) against 29.9 million ($46.7 million) last time.
Profits excluding the exceptional provisions rose 3.7 percent to 28 million pounds ($44 million). Sales from ongoing businesses were up 7.9 percent to 843.1 million pounds ($1.3 billion).

Sears, which has been under pressure to boost profits from its sprawling retail empire, said strong performances from womens fashion and flagship London department store Selfridges were overshadowed by poor trading in home shopping and shoes.
The company set aside 32.5 million pounds ($51 million) to cover the cost of property disposals and debts owed to Sears by Facia, the retailer which collapsed earlier this year.
The charge was partly offset by the release of 7.5 million pounds ($11.8 million) in provisions held over from the previous year, giving a net additional provision of 25 million pounds ($39 million).
